extraction.name: PIQA: Physical Interaction: Question Answering
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset and task for physical commonsense reasoning in natural language, framed as multiple choice question answering where given a physical goal, an agent must choose the most sensible solution between two options.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Annotators were prompted with links to instructables.com across six categories (costume, outside, craft, home, food, and workshop) and asked to extract or be inspired to construct two component tasks: articulatating a physical goal, a valid solution, and a subtly invalid solution (trick). Data was collected in batches of several thousand triples.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Examples with low agreement were removed during validation. Stylistic annotation artifacts and trivial examples were systematically filtered out using the AFLite algorithm, which fine-tuned BERT-Large on 5,000 instances to compute embeddings and used an ensemble of linear classifiers on random data subsets to eliminate instances indicative of the target label. Tokenized examples were truncated at 150 tokens.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdsourced annotators created (goal, valid solution, incorrect solution/trick) triples based on instructables. A qualification HIT containing well-constructed and underspecified pairs was required (>80% accuracy). A diff button in the annotation interface highlighted differences between solutions to improve accuracy and speed. Collected data was validated in batches by other annotators, and annotators with low agreement were disqualified.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Validation was used to remove examples with low agreement, such as those requiring expert-level knowledge rather than commonsense. Human performance was calculated via majority vote among qualified annotators scoring >=90%.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotator pay averaged >15$/hr according to self-reporting on turkerview.com and timing calculations.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Spacy, GPT BPE tokenizer, AFLite, BERT-Large, Hugging Face transformers library
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Reporting bias in language where everyday commonsense properties and atypical uses of objects are rarely explicitly stated; annotators tend toward prototypical solutions without prompting. Annotation artifacts and stylistic biases were removed using AFLite.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Learning physical commonsense from language alone is fundamentally limited without real-world interaction; models struggle with subtle relations, non-prototypical combinations, and certain versatile concepts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking, training, validation, and testing natural language processing models on physical commonsense reasoning.
